Arithmetic, Population and Energy - Prof. Al Bartlett. The most important video you will ever watch in your entire life.

I am watching this video now. I read the first comment by Gareth Ham who has some criticisms. I would like to point out for those considering watching the video that Gareth's objections are, in fact, covered in the video, despite claims that they are not. For example, Al Bartlett points out in the video that, at current growth rates, the human population would eventually take up the entire mass of the Earth. Al also covers resource and production improvements including mathematical examples.

As for the idea of growth throughout the universe, this is quite fanciful, but after watching this video, you will see the problems with this too.

I shall paste his comment here:

Great presentation, and I agree with almost everything within. However, I would suggest that we absolutely do not have an overpopulation problem as of yet (totally separate to population GROWTH), yet we face extreme resource management issues that give the appearance of an overpopulation problem. We have the technology today, to support many times the current population of the earth, and to a very high (higher than current average, or median) standard of living, if only we utilised our technologies to their full capacity. This of course, will never happen within a monetary system, but fortunately, there are realistic alternatives (Resource Based Economy).

*That is where I take issue with the presentation. It does not acknowledge the process of 'ephemeralization', which is in essence, our ability to do more and more, with less and less, over time. When you consider this fact, in combination with the extreme likelihood of our ability in the future (excluding the probability of our extermination between now and then) to be able to utilise the resources of other planets in our solar system, and eventually other solar systems and even galaxies all together, it becomes evident that we do still have some space and time, before we have to curb our population growth,

so long as we rectify the misuse of our resources!﻿*

I think he is missing the point. A common complaint by delusionists is that there is ample food to go around, it is merely a problem of distribution. If he was paying attention and thinking critically he would understand why this is a foolish approach. The value of a thing is determined by how much energy has been expended to create it and move it to where it is being used. Before mass transit, a shoe maker in France did not sell his shoes in Germany. Quite simply, the cost and energy involved in moving the item nullifies all of the profit. The return on investment is zero. If you need to transport your food half way around the world you are as they say 'on a hiding to nothing'. What this means is it is only as of now that we temporarily have the ability to move huge quantities of things around easily that we are under the illusion that it is a simple case of distributing the wealth. As energy becomes more scarce, resources are only able to be moved less.
